place.source_title: Galena Doorways, Sisters of Mercy Convent, 226 North Bench Street

brief: St. Brendan's convent: a one-and-a-half-storey brick building of the early 1840s with stepped-parapet gable ends and chimneys, tall round-headed windows along the side, standing hard against the sidewalk above a stone retaining wall on a sloping street, with a small porch on the uphill end. Record gap: 1 photo only (the HABS doorway survey); massing follows the photo, detailing follows the town's other early brick buildings.

facade.notes: a Galena convent (1843): brick with stepped parapet gable ends and paired chimneys standing proud of the roof, tall round-arched windows and door, a high cut-stone basement; the sidewalk runs below a stone retaining wall; brick neighbours built close; a Model A at the curb (HABS 1930s)

why.note: stepped parapets at the gable ends: party-wall fire stops in a dense brick town
Galena's steep river-bluff streets: lots terraced behind stone walls
